title: Equipment-identity source registry entry
description: Shape of one entry in source_registry.json -- a provenance record for a source of equipment identity/visual data, never itself a grant of usage rights. The nested `rights` object is the only thing that grants anything, only once legalReviewState=REVIEWED, and then only for subjects inside its `rightsScope`: a permission is a question about a specific object, not about a source, so rights.py's `eligible_for(record, use, subject)` requires the object to be named. This schema and rights_decision.schema.json enforce field shape and the evidence matrix's presence/absence obligations; scripts/equipment_identity/rights.py enforces everything a static schema cannot -- resolving and re-hashing the terms snapshot, and every eligibility decision.

sourceId.description: Stable, never reused once a source has ANY history -- other records (future asset/evidence entries) will reference this id.

priority.description: Must be one of the priorities `rights.CANONICAL_PRIORITIES_BY_SOURCE_CLASS` allows for this record's sourceClass -- not freely chosen per record. See core/equipment_identity/p0/SOURCE_PRIORITY.md.

retrievedAt.description: ISO-8601 timestamp this record's canonicalUrl/termsUrl were actually checked, not the record's creation date.

termsUrl.description: URL of the source's actual terms/license page, or null if none is known yet. null here does not imply permission -- rights.legalReviewState still governs.
